review_scope: Bounded source and assertion review at b901326c. Neither whole-clause nor whole-ADR certification. Draft/run statements describe reviewer handoff; current execution and parent qualifications are in findings.json and gate-results.json.

reviewer_record.decision: Namespace-scoped role resolution and attribute precedence follow the element's own namespace and ranked owner semantics.
reviewer_record.review: Retain for the exercised cases. Tests distinguish the root RoleMap from an element namespace's RoleMapNS and route a mapping to another namespace. Attribute priority tests cover selected standard owners, class and inherited/default values. The effective clause equates namespace owner names only when they correspond to Table 376 owner names; do not generalize that to arbitrary expanded URIs.
reviewer_record.residuals: No certification of all Table 376 owners or all §14.8.5 owner-specific attributes.

reviewer_record.decision: Standard structure type names are recognized separately from role-map aliases.
reviewer_record.review: The sampled role-chain and cycle assertions support the implemented walk. ADR scope deliberately separates the type vocabulary from attribute behavior; this shard does not certify every standard type or downstream semantic consumer.
reviewer_record.residuals: Whole-vocabulary certification is outside this bounded audit.

reviewer_record.decision: Attribute attachment, owner ranking, class values, inheritance and defaults are exposed as separate precedence sources.
reviewer_record.review: Retain for the sampled attributes. The tests demonstrate owner-versus-class and class-versus-element cases; EC3 #289's later class-object precedence has a distinct test. A claim that all Table 376 owners or every Table 376/377 attribute is correct would exceed the evidence.
reviewer_record.residuals: External/unrecognized owner behavior and exhaustive per-attribute defaults/inheritability remain bounded.

reviewer_record.decision: Resource limits bound logical structure traversal.
reviewer_record.review: The rationale for limits is sound, and the public Reading::truncated contract explicitly promises that a traversal cut short is not represented as complete. Current structure/logical.rs silently returns at MAX_DEPTH, while structure.rs children()/identified_children() silently take MAX_CHILDREN; only MAX_ELEMENTS sets Walk.truncated. This is a concrete reporting gap. The draft tests accept either complete traversal or an explicit truncation signal; no ISO reader-rejection requirement is inferred.
reviewer_record.residuals: Draft tests not compiled or run under this read-only assignment.

reviewer_record.decision: A circular role-map walk returns a stable known standard role when one is encountered, or reports the unresolved cycle.
reviewer_record.review: The fixture supports the chosen stopping behavior and confirms cycle termination. The standard's NOTE 2 requires a chain to end in a standard type but does not specify a canonical repair for an invalid circular chain, so treat the first-known-role result as an implementation policy for malformed input, not a normative conformance rule.
reviewer_record.residuals: No rejection obligation for a malformed circular role map is claimed.

reviewer_record.decision: Read a structure type in the standard namespace it belongs to, after resolving its role map.
reviewer_record.review: The standard namespace/type routing is represented in current role resolution; EC3 clarifies that an unnamespaced element's final mapped name must be defined by the default namespace. The checked tests cover both namespace-specific map forms and standard-role/cycle outcomes, but this is not a complete audit of every PDF 1.7/PDF 2.0 vocabulary difference or malformed namespace recovery policy.
reviewer_record.residuals: No whole-vocabulary or malformed namespace recovery certification.
